title: Wickens wins in the Nürburgring rain
dek: Robert Wickens won the wet Nürburgring race from seventh on the grid, 2.158 seconds ahead of pole-sitter Augusto Farfus, while Mike Rockenfeller's early rain tyres brought fourth and a 35-point lead.

chapters.title: A title fight on a changeable circuit
text: The DTM's seventh race of ten in 2013 was held at the Nürburgring on Sunday 18 August, on the 3.629-kilometre circuit, with a maximum running time of 75 minutes. The rules called for two mandatory pit stops, and teams could choose between option and standard tyres in the dry.

Mike Rockenfeller arrived as the championship leader. He had won from pole in Moscow a fortnight earlier, 1.303 seconds ahead of Mattias Ekström in an Audi one-two, with Farfus third. That took him to 94 points, 27 clear of Bruno Spengler on 67, with Gary Paffett on 57, Christian Vietoris on 56, Farfus on 48 and Robert Wickens on 45. Spengler, the defending champion, had finished 19th in Moscow, a lap down and without a point, while Paffett's fifth place had been the best Mercedes result.

Wickens arrived with unfinished business. He started the Norisring race from pole and was briefly credited with the win after Mattias Ekström's exclusion, only for the race to be left without an official winner. He was still looking for a first DTM victory.

chapters.title: Farfus on pole, the title rivals off the pace
text: Farfus took pole position with a 1:23.296 in the final single-lap shoot-out. Wittmann of BMW Team MTEK missed it by 0.149 seconds and lined up second. Miguel Molina's Phoenix Audi was third on 1:23.451 and Edoardo Mortara's Rosberg Audi fourth, which put two Audis and two BMWs in the final part.

Behind them came a block of Mercedes. Paffett was fifth, Daniel Juncadella sixth, Wickens seventh and Vietoris eighth, with Mattias Ekström ninth and Spengler tenth, so that the top ten split into four Mercedes, three Audis and three BMWs. The qualifying order was awkward for most of the title contenders. Of the leading six in the standings, Farfus was the only one on the front row, while Rockenfeller was knocked out in the second part of qualifying and lined up 11th, one place ahead of Jamie Green, with Timo Glock 13th, Tambay 14th, Pascal Wehrlein 15th and Joey Hand 16th.

The first part of the session claimed some well-known names. Albuquerque was 17th, two-time champion Timo Scheider 18th and Dirk Werner 19th. Martin Tomczyk, the 2011 champion, would start 20th, Roberto Merhi 21st and Andy Priaulx last of the 22 runners.

chapters.title: Slicks in the rain
text: Rain arrived just as the 22 cars left the pits for the formation lap, and with the field still on slicks the opening lap was chaotic. Farfus led early on from pole, but the first corners cost several contenders dearly. Hand's BMW was out on the spot after a collision, Spengler was hit by rivals more than once and lost time with a damaged car, and Rockenfeller, caught up in an excursion, tumbled down to 20th.
Wittmann, second on the grid, also ran wide in the opening laps and dropped well down the order, ending his chance of a win. The safety car came out to calm the field.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller gambles, Paffett pays
text: Under the safety car Phoenix called Rockenfeller in for rain tyres, making him the first driver to switch. The decision paid off as more rain fell, and he picked off the slick runners to lead by lap six. The catch was that the stop came before the pit window had opened and so did not count as one of the two mandatory stops, which left him needing three in all.

Paffett's HWA crew read it the other way. After about six laps of heavy rain the Mercedes fitted option slicks, a dry-weather choice that proved costly, and he eventually finished a lap down in 17th. Wickens, by contrast, worked steadily forward as the track dried and moved up to second behind Rockenfeller, passing Farfus and Tambay.

chapters.title: Wickens takes the lead and the flag
text: Wickens went ahead as Rockenfeller made his last stop, and crossed the line 2.158 seconds clear of Farfus when the 75-minute limit expired after 47 laps. Vietoris took third for Mercedes, 9.749 seconds behind the winner after starting eighth. Rockenfeller, who had led for most of the afternoon before being passed by all three, finished fourth, 20.524 seconds back.

Tomczyk came from 20th on the grid to fifth, 27.104 behind, to score his first points of the season. Tambay was sixth, Wittmann recovered to seventh, Molina eighth, Green ninth and Wehrlein tenth, who also set the fastest lap, a 1:23.835 on lap 42. Spengler could not defend his place in the top ten with a damaged car and finished 14th, ahead of Werner and Priaulx.
Paffett was 17th, Glock 18th and Merhi 19th, all a lap down, with Glock having been spun round in contact with Juncadella. Juncadella retired after 29 laps and Scheider after eight.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller 35 clear, Wickens a winner at last
text: Wickens called it an incredible, crazy race. He said he had not known what to expect from seventh on the grid, that the pit stops and tyre choice had been perfect, and that he was overjoyed with his first DTM victory. Mercedes motorsport head Toto Wolff said the strategy had worked out perfectly for Wickens and Vietoris, while the different approach tried with Paffett had not worked, which he said could happen.

Farfus said the race had been like a lottery, that he lost a lot of time in the heavy rain early on and could not make it up later, but that second was a great result. BMW motorsport director Jens Marquardt congratulated Mercedes and said the team had run different strategies for Farfus and Wittmann to learn which worked best. He called Tomczyk's drive sensational, and described Spengler's afternoon as frustrating, with the car too badly damaged for him to defend himself late on, though the team would keep fighting in the remaining races.

For Rockenfeller, a bad start to the day turned into a points haul. He thanked Phoenix for the strategy, saying the fourth place was down to the team, and added that he was not yet thinking about the title. Audi's DTM head Dieter Gass called it the most thrilling and spectacular race of the year and praised the decision to change to rain tyres during the safety car and run three stops.

The championship now read Rockenfeller 106, Vietoris 71, Wickens 70, Spengler 67 and Farfus 66, with Paffett on 57, 49 behind the leader. Vietoris had moved up to second, ahead of the winner, and Rockenfeller's lead stood at 35 points with three races to run. Spengler, who had been second before the weekend, was now fourth and 39 points adrift, a single point ahead of Farfus. Paffett's chances of the title were significantly reduced by the tyre error. For BMW, Farfus's runner-up finish, Tomczyk's fifth and Wittmann's recovery to seventh after his early off earned BMW useful points, but none of it closed the gap to the championship leader. The DTM next moved to Oschersleben on 15 September, four weeks later.

facts.t: Rain tyres under the safety car
facts.v: Rockenfeller pitted for rain tyres during the safety car period, before the pit window opened, so the stop did not count as mandatory and he needed three stops.
